name: Gregg Hall
use: Environmental research and technology labs: NOAA cooperative institutes, Environmental Research Group, Hubbard Genome Center, technology-commercialization offices
builtText: 2001 (opened spring 2001 as the Environmental Technology Building)
architect: Lavallee Brensinger Architects; builder Eckman Construction
style: Contemporary brick with a glazed curtain-wall bay and standing-seam roof

renovations.what: Boiler plant upgrade: steam boilers replaced with hydronic boilers and building controls converted (bid notice; date not shown)

facts.text: Became operational in 2001 as an environmental technology building; tenants included NOAA-UNH CICEET, CINEMAR, the Environmental Research Group and the Hubbard Genome Center.
A 40,000 sq ft building south of the Field House, built with $8.5 million in federal funds as part of a planned "Entrepreneurial Campus" quadrangle.
Lavallee Brensinger calls it the first building of the Southeast Quad master plan: four stories with high-bay and wet labs designed for adaptability.

verdict: 2001 brick research building with a glass entrance bay; adaptable labs, no particular presence.
notes: No licensed photo found. Archives reference photo shows a red-brick four-story building with a tall glass curtain-wall entrance bay, grey roof and a dormer arch, among trees. Old row's "dedicated 2004" not confirmed; a search excerpt from a UNH page claimed "dedicated in 1999", which conflicts with the 2001 opening; unresolved. The boiler bid notice date is not shown (search engine said 2022). Tenant list is the archives' and may be dated.
